# Lan Multiplayer (Michitai.Lan) — Full Reference
# https://lan.michitai.com — https://github.com/levandovici/lan-multiplayer
# License: MIT No Attribution (MIT-0). Copyright (c) 2026 Nichita Levandovici.
# This file is optimized for LLM context windows: the complete library
# reference in one document.

## What it is

A LAN multiplayer networking library for game developers, available as:
- a .NET Framework 4.8 class library (dotnet/)
- a drop-in Unity source package (unity/, same API + mobile helpers)
- a standalone C++20 CMake static library (cpp/, wire-compatible)

It provides everything needed to host, discover and join multiplayer sessions
on a local network, optimized for 30-60 FPS state synchronization over
Wi-Fi/LAN. No external servers required.

## Architecture

Client                                  Server
  |  -- UDP broadcast "discover" -->    |   (BroadcastServer, ports 60000-60128)
  |  <-- ServerInfo (name, port) --     |
  |                                     |
  |  ------- TCP connect ---------->    |   (Server, ports 50000-50128)
  |  ------- Terminal commands --->     |   reliable channel (frames, compressed)
  |  <------------- responses -----     |
  |                                     |
  |  ======= UDP state datagrams ==>    |   (UDPChannel, same port as TCP)
  |  <====== BroadcastState =======     |   unreliable, 30-60Hz, latest-wins

Wire protocol (TCP): every message is a frame
  [4-byte LE payload length][1-byte flags][UTF-8 payload]
Flag 0x01 marks a GZip-compressed payload. FrameBuffer decodes partial reads
and multiple frames per read, and rejects frames over Frame.MaxPayloadSize
(32 MB default). UDP datagrams are [1-byte flags][payload]; keep them under
UDPChannel.SafeDatagramSize (1472) to avoid IP fragmentation.

Channel selection:
- Client.Request / Server.Response (TCP): anything that must arrive —
  commands, login, world data
- Client.SendState / Server.BroadcastState (UDP): transient per-frame values
  where a dropped packet is superseded by the next one

## Quick start (C# / Unity)

Start a server and answer discovery probes:

    Multiplayer.Name = "My Game Server";
    Multiplayer.IpAddress = Lan.LocalIPv4Addresses(EPlatform.Standalone)[0];

    Multiplayer.StartServer(
        platform: EPlatform.Standalone,
        serverGameData: new ServerGameData(Guid.NewGuid().ToString()),
        processMessage: (LocatedMessage msg) =>
            new AppMessage(1, "my-game", /* serialized ServerInfo */ "..."),
        receiveRequestsDelayMilliseconds: 500);

Discover servers on the LAN:

    Multiplayer.StartBroadcastClient(
        platform: EPlatform.Standalone,
        request: new AppMessage(1, "my-game", "discover"),
        onReceiveResponse: (LocatedMessage response) => {
            // response.IPEndPoint + payload identify the server
        },
        receiveResponsesMilliseconds: 5000,
        repeatAfterMilliseconds: 5000);

Connect and send commands:

    Multiplayer.IpAddress = serverIp;
    Multiplayer.Port = serverPort;
    Multiplayer.StartClient();

    Multiplayer.Client.OnResponse += (message) => { /* handle reply */ };

    if (Multiplayer.Client.CanRequest)
    {
        Multiplayer.Client.Request(new Message(
            /* serialized */ Terminal.New()
                .Next("login").Arg("user").Arg("pass")
                .Next("get-data")));
    }

Per-frame state over the unreliable channel (call each frame, ~30-60 Hz):

    // client -> server
    Multiplayer.SendState(new Message(JsonUtility.ToJson(myTransform)));

    // server -> all clients that have sent state
    Multiplayer.OnState += (IPEndPoint from, Message msg) => { /* apply */ };
    Multiplayer.BroadcastState(new Message(worldSnapshot));

    // server -> one client
    Multiplayer.SendState(clientEndPoint, new Message(playerSnapshot));

## Tuning knobs and diagnostics

- Compressor.Enabled, Compressor.Threshold (default 256 bytes)
- Frame.MaxPayloadSize (default 32 MB) — corrupt-frame guard
- UDPChannel.SafeDatagramSize (1472) — stay under to avoid IP fragmentation
- Client.PendingRequests, TCPClient.PendingWrites,
  TCPServer.PendingWrites — backpressure indicators
- Client.Send(message) — fire-and-forget TCP send that skips the
  request/response queue
- Multiplayer lifecycle events: OnServerStarted, OnClientStarted, OnState,
  OnServerDiscovered — see docs.php

## Platform notes

- EPlatform flags (Windows, Linux, MacOS, Standalone, Android, IOS, Mobile)
  select the right network code path per platform.
- unity/ adds MobileBroadcastClient/MobileBroadcastServer (UdpClient-based
  discovery for Android/iOS) and Data/JsonStorage.cs.
- cpp/ is a full C++20 port (Michitai::Lan): thread-per-connection I/O,
  std::future async methods, multicast Event<>. Only dependency: miniz
  (gzip). Build: cmake -S cpp -B cpp/build && cmake --build cpp/build.

## Breaking change notice

The transport was rewritten from a "#end#<>#message#" string-delimiter
protocol to a binary length-prefixed frame protocol. Old and new builds
cannot talk to each other — ship matching versions.

## Website / distribution

lan.michitai.com distributes the .NET and Unity packages behind an
email-verification flow (download.php -> send_code.php -> verify.php ->
downloads.php). The site is PHP 7.4+/MySQL; library downloads are free,
MIT-0 licensed, no attribution required.
